requirements.requirement: Parsing, formatting, comparisons and exact timestamp arithmetic
requirements.details: Strict explicit-offset RFC 3339; uppercase separators; nanosecond precision; canonical UTC/fixed offsets; proleptic Gregorian years 0000 through 9999; leap seconds and unknown offsets rejected; comparisons by instant; full-range differences and checked elapsed addition/subtraction without Float or Int truncation.

Bundled IANA 2025b with local and UTC years restricted to 1800 through 2099; strict fixed offsets and exact named zones; no OS or process-local zone inference; reject/earlier/later repeated-time selection; New York and Lord Howe gaps/folds; elapsed-day behavior across DST; Paris historical seconds preserved through parsing/formatting or rejected in RFC 3339 conversion; local parsing cannot silently ignore offset, abbreviation or epoch fields.

requirements.requirement: Signed exact durations and overflow boundaries
requirements.details: Signed i128 nanoseconds, including MIN/MAX; ordered ISO weeks or days/time subset; no calendar months/years; integer units from weeks through nanoseconds; exact String totals; checked sums/differences; canonical zero, unit normalization and fractional trimming.

requirements.requirement: Wall clock, diagnostics and output admission
requirements.details: Capture SystemTime once; deterministic pre/post-epoch helper tests; typed call/source diagnostics and preserved destinations; two-pass bounded formatting using DelayedFormat::write_to instead of its allocating Display implementation; exact temporary argument/result overlap; allocator oracle requires zero large allocation on rejection and exactly one on admission.

requirements.requirement: Catalogue, CLI, quotas, examples and conformance
requirements.details: Sixteen date/time signatures bring the default fixed catalogue to 57. Typed metadata, overrides, normal scope matching, snapshot admission, executed documentation, example 31 and B4 corpus cases are verified.

generated_discovery.note: Discovery verifies expanded configuration; no generated campaign score is claimed.

validation_scope: Full GNU/musl debug/release suites: 1,602 passing tests each. Strict Clippy on both targets, formatting and coverage/mutation helper checks. Fifteen focused semantic mutations executed in an isolated source snapshot against library/CLI unit, date/time and allocation tests.
review_notes: The date/time built-ins share the existing two-pass bounded String writer through a narrow formatter adapter. Calendar formatting streams directly, avoiding the large intermediate allocation in Chrono DelayedFormat Display; an injected Display call is caught by the allocator oracle.

The transition generator expands recurring rules over 1800..2100. Both local and UTC years are checked for named-zone operations rather than extending the terminal offset indefinitely. Fixed zones keep the wider calendar range.

RFC 3339 input is shape-checked before library parsing to prevent silent acceptance of excessive fractional precision and unknown -00:00 offsets. Leap seconds are explicitly unsupported for elapsed POSIX arithmetic.
Local parsing rejects timezone/epoch directives and variable fractional precision before invoking the calendar parser. Repeated instants are ordered explicitly; gaps are never shifted.

The expanded fixed catalogue crosses the older 16 KiB import-cycle allocation observation threshold. That existing fixture now uses longer paths and a 32 KiB threshold, preserving the zero rejected-detail and one admitted-detail allocation oracle. Production limits remain unchanged.

Preliminary integration fixtures used incorrect assignment delimiters and an expected CLI sort order that retained spaces. Both fixtures were corrected to the existing language and normalized-name contracts before the frozen validation matrix.

limits: This sixteen-statement contract does not promise complete Robot Framework DateTime API compatibility.

Named-zone rules use bundled IANA 2025b and years 1800 through 2099; future political changes require a reviewed dependency update. Historical timezone accuracy is limited by available database evidence.
Durations are elapsed POSIX time with nanosecond precision. Leap seconds, calendar months/years and local-calendar-day arithmetic are unsupported.

Output formats explicitly select displayed precision. Minute-only offset directives cannot retain historical offset seconds; %::z is required for those. Local parsing uses a documented narrower directive set.
Wall-clock reads are not monotonic and do not follow paused Tokio timers. Parsing/formatting execute inline with cooperative checks around individual library calls and admitted input sizes.
No Windows/macOS validation, new coverage percentage, complete generated mutation score or performance guarantee is claimed.

root=Path.cwd()

print(f"validation record: {out / 'summary.json'}",flush=True)

record={'complete':False,'started':datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),'revision':subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip(),'input_sha256':{str(p.relative_to(root)):hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in inputs},'checks':[]}
focused=['--test','setup_failure','--test','suite_fixtures','--test','documentation','--test','examples','--test','conformance']
commands=[('gnu-debug-full',['cargo','test','--locked']),('gnu-release-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--release']),('musl-debug-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--target','x86_64-unknown-linux-musl']),('musl-release-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--release','--target','x86_64-unknown-linux-musl']),('clippy-gnu',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('clippy-musl',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--target','x86_64-unknown-linux-musl','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('format',['cargo','fmt','--all','--','--check']),('coverage-helper',['python3','tests/coverage_tools.py']),('mutation-helper',['python3','tests/mutation_tools.py'])]

try:
 for label,command in commands:
  print('running '+label,flush=True)
  log=out/(label+'.log')
  with log.open('w') as stream:
   result=subprocess.run(command,stdout=stream,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=1200,env=dict(os.environ,CARGO_BUILD_JOBS='2'))
  content=log.read_text()
  rows=re.findall(r'test result: (?:ok|FAILED)\. (\d+) passed; (\d+) failed; (\d+) ignored;',content)
  check={'label':label,'command':command,'status':result.returncode,'log':str(log.relative_to(root)),'tests':dict(zip(('passed','failed','ignored'),[sum(int(row[i]) for row in rows) for i in range(3)]))}
  record['checks'].append(check)
  (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2)+'\n')
  print(json.dumps(check),flush=True)

   print(content[-12000:],flush=True)
